paper.title: LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation
claims_from_primary_abstract: semantic segment-level rather than turn-level consolidation
finalized segments encoded into context-independent typed memory records
lightweight structured indexes for query-planned evidence retrieval
reported construction-token reductions versus A-Mem: 86.0% on LoCoMo and 75.9% on LongMemEval-S without higher query-time token usage

source_observations: OnlineSemanticChunker is explicitly LLM-free and keeps one open chunk per session.
The chunker splits at user-bounded exchanges, embeds exchanges, tracks duplicate pending exchanges by turn index, and supports deterministic session_flush finalization.
Default chunk token preferences are 1000 minimum, 1500 target and 2000 hard maximum; oversized exchanges are split and capacity is fail-bounded.
Semantic boundary scoring combines embedding surprise, centroid/tail similarity, cohesion drop and length/turn hazards; cut decisions and reasons are recorded.
CompactSemanticEncoder performs one LLM call per finalized conversation/chunk to extract typed records and disambiguation context.
Encoder reference_context is documented as read-only disambiguation context and not a new evidence source.
MemoryRecord types include fact, preference, event, constraint, procedure, failure_pattern and tool_affordance, with temporal metadata and source session/role/evidence turn range.
SearchPlan supports semantic/pragmatic queries, temporal filters, evidence constraints and independent evidence routes.
The current source therefore materially supports the V2 mechanism shape; the paper's benchmark numbers remain paper claims and were not reproduced in this macrocycle.

cross_research_constraints.finding: Agent memory should be tested on static state, dynamic state, workflow knowledge, environment gotchas and premise awareness over long environment trajectories, not only conversational recall.

cross_research_constraints.source: Beyond Similarity: Trustworthy Memory Search for Personal AI Agents / arXiv:2606.06054
cross_research_constraints.finding: Similarity retrieval is a trust boundary; semantically related memory can cause cross-domain leakage, sycophancy, tool-call drift or memory-induced jailbreaks. Query-conditioned admission can reduce these risks.

strong_reuse: LLM-free semantic boundary detection before expensive memory extraction
batch-finalize coherent segments instead of invoking a model on every turn
explicit evidence routes and temporal constraints in retrieval
recorded boundary diagnostics for later ablation and causal review
do_not_import: a second mutable canonical memory database or truth authority
unscoped semantic similarity as sufficient admission into model context
LLM-generated memory as canonical fact without deterministic provenance/evidence linkage
hard deletion/rewriting semantics that erase canonical source events
paper benchmark credit without F2-specific reproduction

hypothesis: A thin F2-native segment-consolidation layer over immutable UnifiedDB event provenance can reduce memory-construction model calls/tokens while preserving evidence fidelity better than eager per-turn extraction or fixed-window batching.
counterhypotheses: Semantic segmentation can split causally linked tool/action/outcome sequences or merge unrelated events when embedding drift is weak.
Delayed finalization can make critical observations unavailable before a decision boundary.
Derived typed records can become a de facto second truth store if provenance and admission semantics are weak.
Embedding-based retrieval without a trust/admission gate can inject contextually inappropriate memory despite high semantic relevance.
For action-heavy F2 traces, deterministic lifecycle/causal boundaries may outperform conversation-style semantic boundaries.

candidate_f2_shape.name: DerivedMemorySegmentEnvelope
candidate_f2_shape.boundary_precedence: hard causal/lifecycle/effect/restart/generation boundaries override semantic batching; semantic boundary is a bounded optimization within those fences
candidate_f2_shape.retrieval_admission: deterministic project/task/generation/provenance/capability/domain filters before semantic ranking; retrieved memories remain candidate evidence until ContextCompiler admission

next_discriminator.objective: Map the candidate envelope and admission sequence onto exact current WP300/WP301/WP303/WP306 interfaces, preserve UnifiedDB authority, and define an E3/E4 benchmark comparing eager-per-turn, fixed-window, semantic-segment and causal-fenced-semantic segmentation.
negative_controls: same wording with different causal identity
goal transition inside an apparent semantic segment
tool result arriving after session or generation boundary
environment gotcha whose wording is low-similarity to the current query
